audit.whatIsWrong: Every side token from Level 2 to first item was set against the explanation printed beside it. whys[1] through whys[5] all describe Graves taking the lane, yet win[2], win[3] and win[5] read 'Singed' and win[1] read 'Skill'. whys[0] calls Level 1 a wash while win[0] read 'Graves'.
audit.why: Emerald+ win rate is 64.71% for Graves and the packet chart is Skill / Graves x5 / Singed, which matches the written reasoning exactly. Singed's early damage is Poison Trail ticks and one Fling on 8-10s; Graves' level 2-3 magazine plus Q cone out-trades that outright.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Graves / Graves / Graves / Graves / Graves / Singed in both layers.

audit.why: The spike story is right: Graves' level 2-3 magazine window, his 6 (Collateral Damage against a dash-less target), his first item, then Singed's drain-tank scaling. Mirror finding confirms the ult war: both ultimates are 100s at rank 1, but Graves' falls to 80 then 60 while Insanity Potion stays 100 at every rank, so repeat ult windows favour Graves, not Singed.
audit.corrected: Left in place; Insanity Potion's Grievous Wounds added to mid so his 6 is priced too.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mega Adhesive's grounding never appears on the page, and Fling's root condition is only half-stated.
audit.why: Riot text, Singed W: 'Throws a vial of mega adhesive on the ground, slowing and grounding enemies who walk on it.' Grounded means Quickdraw will not fire at all — the escape this whole page is built on simply does not exist while you stand in the glue. Singed E: 'If the target Singed flings lands in his Mega Adhesive, they are also rooted.' That is the entire kill pattern and it was absent.
audit.corrected: Written into early, wants.foe[1], the cooldown block, dosFull[0] and report[5]. Mirrored from the Singed-side audit, which recorded the same interaction from his perspective.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid claims Collateral Damage doubles 'as your own escape'; late credits Graves with 'Bushwhack resistances'.
audit.why: Graves R: 'fires an explosive shell dealing heavy damage to the first champion it hits... explodes dealing damage in a cone.' No displacement, no self-movement — it is not an escape. Bushwhack is not a Graves ability at all; his resists come from True Grit on Quickdraw.
audit.corrected: Both removed. Also added that Insanity Potion makes Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds, which is what actually shuts off Graves' sustain late.

audit.why: Packet flagged 'Use Smoke Screen' as a wrong name — false positive; Smoke Screen is Graves' real W and the page describes it correctly as a slow plus sight-range cut. The one wrong claim is report[10]'s 'smoke blinds', fixed here. Also confirmed from the mirror: End of the Line does not create terrain — that derived flag is a parsing artifact of 'detonates... after colliding with terrain', so no terrain-cut advice was written.
audit.corrected: report[10] corrected; no terrain claim added.

edits.before: "Level 1 is even — Singed just walks up to flick Poison Trail on you, and with only one ability and no E charges yet you can't punish him for it either. The lane turns yours at 2-3: the moment he steps to a minion or commits his Fling, E-in, dump the point-blank 4-shell magazine, and detonate Q's cone on top of him. His early damage is one Fling on cooldown plus Poison Trail ticks, and neither out-trades that burst. The traps to avoid are chasing him into his own poison cloud or standing in it stacking ticks for free, and his Fling tossing you backward into his tower or the minion wave — hold an E charge to dash straight back out."
edits.after: "Level 1 is even — Singed just walks up to flick Poison Trail on you, and with only one ability and no E charges yet you can't punish him for it either. The lane turns yours at 2-3: the moment he steps to a minion or commits his Fling, E-in, dump the point-blank 4-shell magazine, and detonate Q's cone on top of him. His early damage is one Fling every 8-10s plus Poison Trail ticks, and neither out-trades that burst. The real trap is his glue: Mega Adhesive grounds you, and while you stand in it Quickdraw will not fire at all — and a Fling that drops you into it roots you on top of that. Check the ground before you dash."

edits.before: "This is your takeover, but Singed's real plan is to leave — he'll proxy your wave behind the tower so he never has to stand still inside your shell range. When he does step up to Fling or refresh his wave, that's your opening: E-in, magazine, Q-cone, and reset with your second E charge. At 6 your R is the closer — he has no dash, so a kited Singed only has Ghost and his Mega Adhesive slow to survive, and Collateral Damage off a wall catches him through both while doubling as your own escape if his run-down gets scary. Use Smoke Screen on him while you dump shells: it slows him and gut-cuts his vision so he can't peel away clean. Ping your jungler onto his proxy — a stationary, dash-less Singed is a free kill for your mobility."
edits.after: "This is your takeover, but Singed's real plan is to leave — he'll proxy your wave behind the tower so he never has to stand still inside your shell range. When he does step up to Fling or refresh his wave, that's your opening: E-in, magazine, Q-cone, and reset with your second E charge. At 6 your R is the closer — he has no dash, so a kited Singed only has Ghost and his Mega Adhesive slow to survive, and Collateral Damage catches him through both. His 6 matters too: Insanity Potion makes Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds, so your sustain stops paying while it is up. Use Smoke Screen on him while you dump shells: it slows him and cuts his sight range so he can't peel away clean. Ping your jungler onto his proxy — a dash-less Singed is a free kill."

edits.before: "Late game flips to Singed and you have to play around it. Once his drain-tank HP, sustain, and Ghost come online he proxies uncatchably and runs you down between fights — your shells need you in his face, and a full-build Singed just walks through the kiting while his HP outlasts your two-shell magazine and reload. Your True Grit armor and Bushwhack resistances do nothing against his Poison Trail or Fling because those aren't autos and ignore armor on the magic/percent side. Win on tempo: turn your 2-3 and first-item lead into plates, kills, and objectives so the game is decided before his scaling makes the extended 1v1 his."
edits.after: "Late game flips to Singed and you have to play around it. Once his drain-tank HP, sustain, and Ghost come online he proxies uncatchably and runs you down between fights — your shells need you in his face, and a full-build Singed just walks through the kiting while his HP outlasts your two-shell magazine and reload. True Grit's armor does nothing against Poison Trail's magic ticks, and Insanity Potion makes that poison apply Grievous Wounds so your sustain stops paying too. Win on tempo: turn your 2-3 and first-item lead into plates, kills, and objectives so the game is decided before his scaling makes the extended 1v1 his."

notes: MIRROR CONFLICT, flagged rather than forced: the Singed-side audit deliberately made no level-chart edits, noting that champ-data/content/singed.js and singed.full.js agree with each other and with a 51.02% Emerald+ figure, while this side's packet reports 64.71% for Graves. I still fixed the Graves page because its side tokens contradicted the whys printed directly beneath them — that is an internal error regardless of which win rate is authoritative. If the two pages end up disagreeing, mirror-fix.js should resolve toward the packet chart used here. Biggest content win: Mega Adhesive's grounding, which was absent from the whole page even though it turns off Quickdraw, the escape every other line depends on.
